title: The AI boom: rational enthusiasm or the next dot-com bubble?
gist: The ECB states outright that a correction in US equity valuations is likely, with S&P 500 CAPE near its historical peak, and argues the call holds whether or not today's AI prices are rational – because as AI adoption goes economy-wide the risk premium rises and historically overwhelms the cash-flow good news. The euro area's own tech valuations look tame, but euro area households carry roughly €440 billion of US tech equity exposure via low-cost ETFs and index trackers, and policymakers have far less rate-cut and fiscal room to cushion a fallout than in 2000.

insights.claim: The ECB states that economic research on past technological revolutions points to a likely correction of current stock market valuations – an unusually explicit equity-valuation warning from a central bank.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: A named central-bank correction call is a policy-reaction-function signal: expect more ECB financial-stability commentary on AI concentration, and treat it as a soft-tail-hedge prompt rather than a timing signal.
insights.quote: We argue that economic research on past technological revolutions points to a worrisome conclusion: a correction of current stock market valuations is likely.
insights.locator: Valuations on the US stock market, as measured

insights.claim: US equity valuations measured by the Shiller CAPE ratio are currently close to their historical peak, while euro area CAPE has risen to a lesser extent, using monthly data from 1980 to 2026 on the S&P Composite and Euro Stoxx 50.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: The valuation gap is the core of the trade: it argues for underweighting US mega-cap tech multiples relative to euro area equities on a valuation-risk basis.
insights.locator: Valuations on the US stock market, as measured by the CAPE ratio

insights.claim: The case for expecting an equity correction does not depend on whether today's prices are rational or irrational – both the rational option-value view and the behavioural bubble view predict boom then pullback.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Removes the usual escape hatch for bulls: 'AI is real, therefore no crash' is a non-sequitur, so hedging cannot be deferred until a bubble is proven.
insights.quote: the case for expecting a correction is not dependent on whether today’s prices are rational or irrational
insights.locator: Both views imply a boom followed by a correction

insights.claim: The ECB concedes a correction is not a call for a lower long-run ceiling: if AI proves transformative enough, valuations could be much higher in the future even after the correction, and it is impossible to know in advance where we stand on that path.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Argues for buying drawdown protection rather than structurally shorting AI – a post-correction re-rating higher is explicitly on the table.
insights.quote: If AI proves to be transformative enough, valuations could still be much higher in the future, even after a correction.
insights.locator: This does not mean that today’s prices represent a ceiling

insights.claim: The exact timing of a technology boom-bust is unknowable in advance and such patterns are only identifiable with hindsight, per the ECB's own framing.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Rules out market-timing on this thesis; favours convex, cheap, long-dated hedges and position-sizing discipline over exit calls.
insights.quote: The exact timing is unknowable in advance. These boom-bust patterns are only identifiable with hindsight.
insights.locator: The exact timing is unknowable in advance

insights.claim: Under the rational Pastor-Veronesi view, extreme uncertainty about a new technology's productivity creates an 'option value' that lifts early adopters' price-to-earnings ratios, and the ECB uses Nvidia's roughly 20-fold share price rise since 2022 as the worked example of investors pricing the chance it becomes 'the next Google'.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Reframes Nvidia's multiple as an option premium on an unbounded upside, which means it decays as uncertainty resolves – even if the company keeps winning.
insights.quote: Why has Nvidia’s share price risen 20-fold since 2022? Because investors rationally perceived that the company would become the next Google – with a highly uncertain and potentially large upside.

insights.claim: The behavioural channel means the downside is asymmetric: when overconfidence fades, prices can fall even more sharply than in the rational scenario.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Fat-tail justification for paying up for out-of-the-money protection rather than assuming an orderly de-rating.
insights.quote: When overconfidence fades, prices can fall even more sharply than in the rational scenario.
insights.locator: The second explanation for technology-driven boom and bust is the behavioural view

insights.claim: The ECB points to four historical precedents where a genuinely transformative technology attracted investment and adopters' valuations rose strongly before falling sharply: 19th century railways, 1920s electricity and radio, and the 1990s internet/dot-com era.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Base-rate anchor: technology being real has never been sufficient to prevent a valuation bust, so 'this time the tech works' is not a bull argument.
insights.locator: Why do technological revolutions so often end in a boom and bust?

themes.theme: Risk premium regime shift from sector to economy-wide

insights.claim: The key mechanism for a correction even in success is a shift in the nature of uncertainty from 'single sector' to 'entire economy': while AI is a small-scale experiment its risk is diversifiable, but as adoption spreads the same uncertainty becomes economy-wide, undiversifiable, and investors demand a higher risk premium.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: The trigger to watch is broad AI adoption itself, not an AI failure – rising adoption rates are the signal that the discount rate is about to reprice.
insights.locator: Even if the technology succeeds, stock prices may eventually fall

insights.claim: Adoption is good news for cash flows but the rising risk premium works the other way and historically tends to prevail, unless profit growth is strong enough to compensate.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Gives the specific escape condition to monitor: only exceptionally strong realised AI profit growth can offset the discount-rate drag, so earnings-delivery vs multiple-compression is the live scoreboard.
insights.quote: Adoption itself is good news for cash flows, but the rising risk premium has the opposite effect and tends to prevail historically
insights.locator: However, this does not necessarily mean that profits will fall

insights.claim: Euro area households have around €440 billion of exposure to US technology equities, increasingly via low-cost ETFs, and the ECB says they hold it without necessarily being aware of the associated concentration risk.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Quantifies the euro area retail wealth channel; a Mag7 drawdown maps directly onto household balance sheets and therefore euro area consumption.
insights.quote: Euro area households, which are increasingly channelling funds into low-cost ETFs, have around €440 billion of exposures to US technology equities without necessarily being aware of the associated concentration risk.
insights.locator: How exposed is the euro area to a fall in Mag7 prices?

insights.claim: Most euro area exposure to the Magnificent Seven – Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Tesla, Meta Platforms, Microsoft and NVIDIA – runs through investment funds (mutual funds and ETFs) rather than direct holdings, with insurance companies and pension funds also holding significant exposures (Q3 2025 market values).
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Passive index dominance means euro area investors are long US mega-cap tech by default; the practical hedge is index-level, not stock-level.
insights.locator: The dominance of the Mag7 on widely held global indices

insights.claim: The fund-based ownership structure is itself an amplification channel: a sharp correction forces funds to sell liquid holdings first and then distressed assets if it persists, pushing valuations lower and triggering further redemptions.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Predicts contagion into non-tech liquid assets first during an AI selloff – watch for indiscriminate selling of liquid euro area holdings as the early tell.
insights.quote: This is why a Mag7 correction is a question of financial stability for the euro area, rather than just a private one.
insights.locator: This fund-based structure is itself a transmission channel

insights.claim: The ECB flags that, unlike during the dot-com episode, today's starting point leaves markedly less room to cut interest rates or use fiscal policy to cushion the fallout, making an equity correction coinciding with broader market instability the more severe scenario.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: The implied put is thinner than in 2000: assume a slower, shallower policy response to an AI drawdown and price duration/credit hedges accordingly.
insights.quote: unlike in the dot-com episode, today’s starting point leaves markedly less room to cut interest rates or use fiscal policy to cushion the fallout
insights.locator: The more severe scenario is not the equity correction on its own

themes.theme: Euro area home-grown risk looks contained

insights.claim: Euro area valuation metrics such as price-to-earnings ratios remain considerably lower than in the United States, and euro area stock markets are dominated by 'old economy' stocks showing little of the AI excitement seen in the US Mag7, which reduces the risk of a home-grown correction.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Supports a relative-value long euro area / short US tech-multiple expression, with the caveat that it is a relative not absolute shield.
insights.locator: Is there overexuberance in euro area stock markets?

insights.claim: The euro area ICT sector looks structurally healthier than during the dot-com bubble: productivity and markups in the sector are rising, the business climate in euro area digital services does not seem exuberant, and firms' AI adoption is rising notably only a few years after ChatGPT's 2022 launch.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Rising markups plus rising adoption without valuation exuberance is the setup where euro area digital names can deliver earnings without a multiple to defend.
insights.locator: The euro area macroeconomic environment in the information and communication technology sector

insights.claim: The overall increase in euro area digital investment over the past decade was more than three times the cumulative growth in GDP over the same period, indicating a profound real digital transformation running alongside the market-valuation story.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: The real-economy capex trend is a separate, more durable exposure than the equity multiple – supportive for euro area digital-infrastructure and enterprise-software suppliers even through a US de-rating.
insights.quote: The overall increase in digital investment in the euro area over the past decade was more than three times the cumulative growth in GDP over that period.
insights.locator: The global AI boom has also sparked an ongoing and profound digital transformation

insights.claim: Because euro area and US stock markets have historically been very highly correlated, a US AI correction would transmit beyond markets into euro area sentiment, financing conditions and hiring – the ECB's conclusion is that a US AI fallout would not remain a US problem.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Kills the 'cheap euro area equities are a safe haven from AI' argument and puts euro area cyclicals, credit spreads and labour data in the transmission path.
insights.quote: A US AI fallout would not remain a US problem.
